extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (agents/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for making and documenting rejections under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103 (obviousness), including provisional rejections based on copending applications, double patenting issues, use of form paragraphs, and the special pre-AIA 103(b) biotechnology-process election. Intended to direct examiner practice and inform applicants of options to overcome rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting rejections and terminal disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Double patenting rejections prevent an organization from obtaining two or more patents with different expiration dates covering nearly identical subject matter. Double patenting rejections can be overcome in certain circumstances by disclaiming, pursuant to 37 CFR 1.321, the terminal portion of the term of the later patent and including in the disclaimer a provision that the patent shall be enforceable only for and during the period the patent is commonly owned with the application or patent which formed the basis for the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP § 804 provides further guidance. For rejection based on a non-commonly owned patent (treated as commonly owned pursuant to the CREATE Act), the double patenting rejection may be obviated by filing a terminal disclaimer in accordance with 37 CFR 1.321(d). Provisional double patenting rejections may be made where the prior art is a copending application; a terminal disclaimer plus an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(c) may overcome double patenting when the earlier file has been published or matured into a patent. Examples in the text (Examples 1–5) illustrate when provisional double patenting and 35 U.S.C. 103 rejections arise and how terminal disclaimers and evidence of common ownership affect results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) using provisional prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two applications of different inventive entities are copending, not published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b), and the filing dates differ, a provisional rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) based on provisional prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) should be made in the later filed application unless the application has been excluded under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such provisional rejections alert the applicant that an actual rejection on the same ground may occur if one application issues, and give the applicant an opportunity to act. The provisional rejection is applied to copending applications having different effective filing dates wherein each application has a common assignee or a common inventor. The earlier filed application, if patented or published, would constitute prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e). The rejection is provisional because the subject matter and the prior art are pending applications. See MPEP §§ 2136.01 and 2146.03 for procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to overcome a provisional 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection (options A–E)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection can be overcome by: (A) arguing patentability over the earlier filed application; (B) combining the subject matter of the copending applications into a single application claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 and abandoning the copending applications; (C) filing an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.132 showing derivation; (D) filing an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(a) showing a date of invention prior to the effective U.S. filing date of the copending application; or (E) for applications pending on or after December 10, 2004, showing that the prior art and the claimed invention were owned by the same person (or subject to obligation of assignment) at the time the invention was made, or that the subject matter is disqualified under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) (joint research agreement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note for (B): a claim in a subsequently filed application relying on a combination of prior applications may not get the benefit of an earlier filing date under 35 U.S.C. 120 if the earlier filed application does not contain a disclosure which complies with 35 U.S.C. 112 for the claim. See Studiengesellschaft Kohle and MPEP cross-references. For (C) and (D) see MPEP §§ 715.01(a), 715.01(c), 716.10 and 715. For (E) see MPEP § 2146. Where interfering subject matter under 37 CFR 41.203(a) is claimed, a terminal disclaimer and an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(c) may be used to overcome a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection in common ownership situations if the earlier filed application has been published or matured into a patent (see MPEP § 718).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and effect of 35 U.S.C. 121 on divisional/continuation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provisional rejection is made and the copending applications are combined into a single application and the resulting single application is subject to a restriction requirement, the divisional application would not be subject to a provisional or actual rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 since the provisions of 35 U.S.C. 121 preclude the use of a patent issuing therefrom as a reference against the resulting application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation-in-part practice and entitlement to 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit is noted — the continuation-in-part is entitled to 120 benefit of each of the prior applications. Example 2 illustrates these principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(b) biotechnology-process election requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(b) provides that a biotechnological process using or resulting in a composition of matter that is novel under section 102 and nonobvious under subsection (a) shall be considered nonobvious if (1) claims to the process and the composition of matter are contained in either the same application or in separate applications having the same effective filing date; and (2) the composition of matter, and the process at the time it was invented, were owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP summarizes the statutory requirements as: (A) process and composition in same application or in separate applications with same effective filing date; (B) both owned or under obligation to assign to same person at time process was invented; (C) patent on process must also contain claims to the composition or, if composition claimed in another patent, patents must expire the same date; (D) the process must fall within the statutory definition of biotechnological process; and (E) a timely election must be made by petition under 37 CFR 1.182. Election timing guidance: normally timely if made no later than the earlier of payment of issue fee or filing an appeal brief, with special rules for applications pending around March–June 1996. Petition must establish all statutory requirements are satisfied. See MPEP § 2159 for applicability and case law discussion (Ochiai, Brouwer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.06: Notice re prior art available under both pre-AIA and AIA
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event the determination of the status of the application as subject to AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 (or as subject to pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103) is incorrect, any correction of the statutory basis for the rejection will not be considered a new ground of rejection if the prior art relied upon, and the rationale supporting the rejection, would be the same under either status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) This form paragraph must be used in all Office Actions when a prior art rejection is made in an application with an actual filing date on or after March 16, 2013, that claims priority to, or the benefit of, an application filed before March 16, 2013. (2) This form paragraph should only be used ONCE in an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.20.fti: Statement of Statutory Basis, Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotation of pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a): 'A patent may not be obtained though the invention is not identically disclosed or described as set forth in section 102, if the differences between the subject matter sought to be patented and the prior art are such that the subject matter as a whole would have been obvious at the time the invention was made to a person having ordinary skill in the art to which said subject matter pertains. Patentability shall not be negatived by the manner in which the invention was made.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) The statute is not to be cited in all Office actions — required only in first actions on the merits employing pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) and final rejections. Where the statute is being applied but not cited in an action on the merits, use paragraph 7.103. (2) This form paragraph should only be used ONCE in a given Office action. (3) This paragraph must precede form paragraphs 7.20.01.fti - 7.22.fti when used to cite the statute in first actions and final rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.20.01.fti: Pre-AIA 103(a) rejection using prior art under pre-AIA 102(e)/(f)/(g) not disqualified under 103(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant has provided a submission that the invention was owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same entity as [1] at the time this invention was made, or was subject to a joint research agreement. However, reference [2] qualifies as prior art under another subsection of pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102, and therefore is not disqualified as prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c. Applicant may overcome the applied art either by a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that the invention disclosed therein was derived from the inventor of this application, or by antedating the applied art under 37 CFR 1.131(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) This paragraph must be included following form paragraph 7.20.fti in all actions containing rejections under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) using art that is disqualified under pre-AIA 103(c) using pre-AIA 102(e)/(f)/(g), but which qualifies under another section of pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102. (2) In bracket 1, identify the common assignee. (3) In bracket 2, identify the reference which has been disqualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.20.02.fti: Joint inventors, common ownership presumed
rubrics_metrics.description: This application currently names joint inventors. In considering patentability of the claims under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a), the examiner presumes that the subject matter of the various claims was commonly owned at the time any inventions covered therein were made absent any evidence to the contrary. Applicant is advised of the obligation under 37 CFR 1.56 to point out inventor and invention dates of each claim that was not commonly owned at the time a later invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: This paragraph must be used in all applications with joint inventors (unless the claims are clearly restricted to only one claimed invention, e.g., only a single claim is presented).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.20.04.fti: Attempted disqualification under 103(c) using common ownership or assignment — ineffective
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant has attempted to disqualify reference [1] under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) by showing that the invention was owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same entity as [2] at the time this invention was made. However, applicant has failed to provide a statement that the application and the reference were owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same person at the time the invention was made in a conspicuous manner, and therefore, the reference is not disqualified as prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a). Applicant must file the required submission in order to properly disqualify the reference under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include this paragraph in all actions containing rejections under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) where an attempt has been made to disqualify the reference under 103(c) but the applicant has not provided a proper statement indicating common ownership or assignment at the time the invention was made. Applicant may still overcome the art by a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 or by antedating under 37 CFR 1.131(a). Identify the commonly owned applied art in brackets 1 and 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.20.05.fti: Attempted disqualification under 103(c) using joint research agreement — ineffective
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant has attempted to disqualify reference [1] under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) by showing that the invention was subject to a joint research agreement at the time this invention was made. However, applicant has failed to [2]. Applicant must file the missing requirements in order to properly disqualify the reference under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must be included in all actions containing rejections under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) where an attempt was made to disqualify the reference under 103(c) via a JRA but the disqualification attempt is ineffective. In bracket 1, identify the reference sought to be disqualified; in bracket 2, identify the reason(s) the attempt is ineffective (e.g., statutory noncompliance, failure to submit required statement, failure to amend specification to include names of parties to the JRA). See 37 CFR 1.71(g), 1.104(c), and MPEP § 2146.02(III). Applicant may still antedate or show derivation as other remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.21.fti: Rejection, Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable over [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) This paragraph must be preceded by either form paragraph 7.20.fti or 7.103. (2) An explanation of the rejection must follow this form paragraph (see MPEP § 2144). (3) If the rejection relies upon prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e), use pre-AIA 102(e) as amended by the AIPA to determine the reference's prior art date unless the reference is a U.S. patent issued directly/indirectly from an international application with an international filing date prior to Nov 29, 2000 — see related guidance. (4) If the applicability of this rejection prevents the reference from being disqualified under 103(c), form paragraph 7.20.01.fti must follow. (5) If this rejection is a provisional 103(a) rejection based upon a copending application that would comprise prior art under 102(e) if patented or published, use form paragraph 7.21.01.fti instead. (6–7) Instructions for bracket entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.21.01.fti: Provisional rejection template (common assignee/applicant/joint inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are provisionally rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being obvious over copending Application No. [2] which has a common [3] with the instant application. Based upon the earlier effective U.S. filing date of the copending application, it would constitute prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) if published or patented. This provisional rejection ... is based upon a presumption of future publication or patenting of the copending application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph is used to provisionally reject claims not patentably distinct from disclosure in a copending application having an earlier U.S. filing date and a common assignee, common applicant (35 U.S.C. 118), or at least one common joint inventor. Do not use when copending application is disqualified under 103(c). Use pre-AIA 102(e)/pre-AIPA 102(e) rules to determine prior art date as appropriate. If claimed invention is fully disclosed in copending application, use paragraph 7.15.01.fti. Insert claim numbers, application number, and specify --assignee--, --applicant--, or --joint inventor-- in brackets. This provisional rejection might be overcome by 37 CFR 1.132, 1.131(a), or showing disqualification under 103(c). If not patentably distinct, make provisional obviousness double patenting rejection using form paragraphs 8.33 and 8.37. Additional rejection under 7.21.fti should be made when (a) evidence indicates the copending application is also prior art under 102(f) or (g); and (b) the copending application has not been disqualified under 103(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.21.02.fti: Rejection using reference with common assignee/applicant/joint inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being obvious over [2]. The applied reference has a common [3] with the instant application. Based upon the earlier effective U.S. filing date of the reference, it constitutes prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection might be overcome by: (1) a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the reference was derived from the inventor of this application; (2) a showing of a date of invention for the claimed subject matter prior to the effective U.S. filing date of the reference under 37 CFR 1.131(a); or (3) an oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(c) stating current common ownership and that the inventive entity named is the prior inventor under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 104 (as in effect on March 15, 2013), together with a terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321(c). This paragraph should not be used if the reference qualifies as prior art under 102(a) or (b) or is disqualified under 103(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.22.fti: Rejection, pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a), further in view of
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable over [2] as applied to claim [3] above, and further in view of [4].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.21.fti. An explanation of the rejection must follow (see MPEP § 2144). If the rejection relies upon prior art under pre-AIA 102(e), follow the AIPA/prior art date determination rules described elsewhere. Insert appropriate bracketed references and explanation of how the additional reference is applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for obviousness (Graham factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: The factual inquiries for establishing a background for determining obviousness under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) are summarized as follows: 1. Determining the scope and contents of the prior art. 2. Ascertaining the differences between the prior art and the claims at issue. 3. Resolving the level of ordinary skill in the pertinent art. 4. Considering objective evidence present in the application indicating obviousness or nonobviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph (7.23.fti) may be used, if appropriate, in response to an argument regarding the applicability of the factors for determining obviousness. See MPEP § 2144 for requirements to explain the combination and rationale when rejecting under 103(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.27.fti: Combined rejection under pre-AIA 102 and 103(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102([2]) as anticipated by or, in the alternative, under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as obvious over [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when anticipation alternative or obviousness alternative is appropriate. Follow standard explanation requirements for both 102 and 103 rejections and include appropriate bracketed references and explanations as required by MPEP § 2144 and related form paragraph notes.
